The fixed <1.5 mm repeatability rule applies to new geometry-qualified validation windows; existing saved models remain loadable without retroactive certification.

With an explicit advanced travel policy, temporary live acceleration reductions can invalidate an earlier admissible plan; acceleration is never raised automatically.
Admitted 75 mm/s moving/no-motion traces use constructed sensor delivery and fake clocks; no real sensor/MCU/host timing or higher-speed hardware behavior was qualified.
Default installation preserves the currently configured speed; it does not restore a historical value from old backups or auto-tune timing/acceleration.
The configured 0.2 g quiet floor and native 20% rule have not been qualified on hardware; modeled ranges are synthetic and do not establish a physical sensor-noise cause or fix.

The conservative motion/direction correction assumes future stationary disturbance stays within the observed accepted-reference envelope; arbitrary later bias or disturbances are not bounded by these fixtures.
Expanded references can leave too little evidence to prove real low-speed motion; the unchanged no_motion deadline then fails closed without automatically changing speed or acceleration.

The ideal true-motion fixture uses 4000 mm/s^2 because an ideal 5000 mm/s^2 sample is already above the unchanged 0.5 g impact threshold; this is a synthetic design choice, not a requested printer retune.

Raising a configured travel budget authorizes more nominal commanded travel before a host stop request; it does not measure actual contact force, physical stopping distance, transport delay or missed steps.
No plugin distance/speed ceiling applies when report/startup travel settings are absent; this does not guarantee a successful physical home at every configured speed.
Explicit advanced travel limits remain bounded to 0.1..2.0 mm reporting and 0.1..5.0 mm startup; these engineering ranges are not physical stopping-distance certifications.
The 1.5 mm rule is a strict ten-validation-home repeatability range per axis, not an impact threshold, sample-latency distance or guaranteed stopping distance.
validation_reason: One final combined offline run after independent review. Configured sensor report/startup travel policies are disabled when absent, represented by None/null rather than infinity. Default 75 and 100 mm/s plans connect, preflight and prepare without changing configured speed, sample age, interval or acceleration. Explicit finite bounded report/startup settings remain independently enforced with strict comparisons and final preparation rechecks. All effective/derived numeric values must remain finite; status and replay fallbacks handle absent policies without invalid JSON. Actual stale/missing/frozen/data-error and startup no_motion handling, conservative baseline movement/direction proof and raw impacts are unchanged. The workflow source is byte-identical to the published base: calibration still requires ten qualified validation homes with strict max-minus-min travel below 1.5 mm separately per axis. Installer fixtures cover the X75/Y50 target without budget flags, configured-speed preservation, explicit opt-ins, retained-axis checks and valid undo. The harness numeric getter models absent optional defaults without accepting explicit invalid None values. No private user log or raw samples are included.
